Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Priorities

The manifesto establishes five national missions: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, breaking barriers to opportunity, and NHS reform.

## Economic Policy

Labour commits to fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt by the fifth forecast year. Corporation tax will be capped at 25%. The party pledges no increases to Income Tax, National Insurance, or VAT.

Key economic initiatives include:
- A National Wealth Fund (£7.3 billion) for industrial investment
- An Industrial Strategy Council on statutory footing
- Business rates reform in England
- A ten-year infrastructure strategy
- Planning system overhaul to enable 1.5 million new homes

## Energy and Environment

Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, will receive £8.3 billion. The target is zero-carbon electricity by 2030 through expanded wind, solar, and nuclear power. No new oil and gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing licences continue. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion for home energy upgrades.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubled CT/MRI scanners, and 8,500 new mental health staff. Education plans feature 6,500 new teachers, free primary school breakfast clubs, and ending VAT exemptions for private schools.

## Immigration and Borders

A Border Security Command will replace the Rwanda scheme. Additional caseworkers will address asylum backlogs. The points-based immigration system will be reformed alongside skills policy.

## Employment

Legislation within 100 days will ban exploitative zero-hours contracts, end fire-and-rehire practices, and establish day-one employment rights. The minimum wage will account for living costs.

## Constitutional Reform

Hereditary peers will lose voting rights. A mandatory retirement age of 80 will apply to Lords members. Voting age drops to 16. An Ethics and Integrity Commission will oversee ministerial standards.

## Foreign Policy

NATO commitment remains absolute, with a Strategic Defence Review planned. The party seeks improved EU relations without rejoining the single market or customs union, pursuing veterinary agreements and security cooperation.
